history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED — no independent web source identifies a distinct 'Panch Mandir' at Surajkund. This file documents the most likely referent: the shrine/hot-spring complex at Surajkund (Surajkund Dhaam), the natural hot springs in Belkapi gram panchayat (Surujkhurd), Barkatha block, Hazaribagh district — CSV town 'Hazaribag' corrected. Surajkund (also called Surya Kund) is claimed to be India's hottest spring, with a surface temperature of about 87 °C (189 °F) per the Jharkhand government and Wikipedia; it has five kunds (Surya, Lakshman, Brahm, Ram, Sita). The site is listed on Justdial under Religious Places with a 4.2 rating. Whether the CSV row intends this complex or a separate temple could not be established — verify against the master CSV.

name: Panch Mandir, Surajkund
town_description: Surajkund is a hot-spring complex in Belkapi gram panchayat (listed as Surujkhurd on directories) of Barkatha block in Barhi subdivision, Hazaribagh district, Jharkhand. The site centres on natural sulphur hot springs said to be the hottest in India, surrounded by forested hills. It functions as both a pilgrimage spot and a tourist attraction, about 72 km from Hazaribagh city on NH-2 (the old Grand Trunk Road).
